epistemic_class: every interface and specification below is INFERRED, not official

problems.title: Organization Report Chain

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Each row lists a manager followed by that manager's direct reports (rows in any order; each manager heads at most one row; exactly one top-level manager; the rows form one tree). "Printing" is modelled as returning the lines: a pre-order walk from the top manager, visiting direct reports in their listed order, each line being two spaces per depth level followed by the name.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Exact print format (indent width/marker) and whether children are re-ordered are not in the preview; chosen: two spaces per level, listed order.

problems.title: Organization Report Chain

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Same tree and line order as variant 1, but each line ends with " (k)" where k is the employee's total number of direct and indirect reports.
problems.inference_uncertainty: The follow-up content of variant 2 is not visible; a subtree report count is an inference from the "report chain" title.

problems.title: Organization Report Chain

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Return the reporting chain from the top-level manager down to the named employee, inclusive at both ends. The employee is guaranteed to exist.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Direction of the chain (top-down chosen) and whether endpoints are included are guesses.

problems.title: Organization Report Chain

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Return the deepest employee whose own sub-hierarchy (including the employee) contains both named employees; one of them may be the answer, and equal names return that name.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Entirely inferred follow-up (lowest common manager); whether an employee counts as their own manager is a guess.

problems.title: Pivot Table Profit Analyzer

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: First row is the header (contains order_id, cost, sell_price, product, date plus optional extra columns, any order). Profit of an order is sell_price minus cost (non-negative decimal strings with at most two fractional digits). Return a pivot table: header row ["product", months...] with every YYYY-MM month that appears, ascending; then one row per product (ascending, code-unit order) holding the total profit for that month as a fixed two-decimal string (negative sign when negative; "0.00" when no orders).
problems.inference_uncertainty: The preview stops before the requested output; the product x month profit layout, amount format and sort orders are all inferred.

problems.title: Price Percentile Cutoff

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Each record "price,count" adds count transactions at price cents; equal prices combine. For integer percentile p in [1,100], return the smallest price P such that at least p percent of all transactions are priced at or below P (nearest-rank: cumulative*100 >= p*total).
problems.inference_uncertainty: Percentile definition (nearest-rank vs interpolation) and the returned quantity (price vs count above cutoff) are inferred.

problems.title: Pythagorean Triples

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Tree on nodes 0..n-1 given by edge arrays. Count nodes u whose distances to x, y and z, after sorting into a<=b<=c, satisfy a*a + b*b == c*c. Zero distances are allowed (so a=0, b=c counts).
problems.inference_uncertainty: The three query nodes x, y, z and the treatment of zero distances are inferred; the preview only defines the tree and dist.

problems.title: Query Log  Matching

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Events are "Q: <words>" or "L: <words>" (lowercase alphanumeric words separated by single spaces). Each query gets the next id starting at 1 and emits "ACK: <phrase>; ID=<id>". A log emits "M: <message>; Q=<ids>" listing, ascending and comma-separated, every earlier query whose distinct words all occur among the log's words; a log with no match emits nothing.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Output strings, id numbering and the all-words-present matching rule are inferred from the common form of this exercise; the preview shows only the event syntax.

problems.title: Range Negate Data Updates

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Apply every 1-based inclusive range negation in order and return the resulting array as a new list.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Whether the answer is the final array (chosen) or an aggregate such as its sum is not visible.

problems.title: Remove Prefix String

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Given unique lowercase words, keep exactly those that are not a strict prefix of another word, in input order.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Low: the preview states the rule; alphabet and size bounds are inferred.

problems.title: Reverse Count and Say

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: The encoding replaces every maximal run of one digit by its length (1 to 99, written without leading zeros) followed by the digit. Return every non-empty digit string whose encoding equals the input, sorted ascending; return an empty list if none.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Whether all decodings or a single one are requested, the output order, and the 99 cap on run length are inferred.

problems.title: Reversi Move Simulation

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Return a new board after trying to place player at (row, col). The move is legal only if the cell is empty and at least one of the eight directions has one or more opponent pieces immediately followed by a player piece; then the piece is placed and all such bracketed opponent pieces flip. An illegal move returns an unchanged copy.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Handling of illegal moves (unchanged copy chosen, versus an error value) is inferred.

problems.title: Shopping Cart Checkout

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: A record is valid when it splits on "|" into exactly four fields, sku and name are non-empty, and quantity and unit price are digit-only strings (leading zeros allowed; signs, decimals or spaces make it invalid). Return [total quantity, total cost in cents] over valid records.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Return shape ([quantity, cents]) and the exact integer grammar are inferred.

problems.title: Shopping Cart Checkout

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Same validity rule. Aggregate valid records by sku and return "<sku>|<name>|<total quantity>|<total cents>" lines sorted by sku (code-unit order); name is from the sku's first valid record.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Entirely inferred follow-up (per-SKU aggregation, name choice, ordering).

problems.title: Shopping Cart Checkout

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Same validity rule and line format as variant 2; return the k sku lines with the largest total cost, ties by sku ascending (all if fewer than k).
problems.inference_uncertainty: Entirely inferred follow-up (ranking key, tie rule, k parameter).

problems.title: Simulate a Deterministic Finite Automaton

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: The preview's fixed automaton diagram is not visible, so the automaton is injected: transitions[s] = [next state on "a", next state on "b"]. Run from start over input (possibly empty) and return whether the final state is accepting.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Highest: the actual fixed DFA is unknown; this variant is a generalisation, not the original question.

problems.title: Snapshot Set Iterator

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Integer set. add/remove return whether the set changed; a re-added value moves to the end of insertion order. getIterator snapshots the current members in insertion order and returns an id (0, 1, ...); hasNext/next walk that snapshot, unaffected by later changes. Iterator objects are modelled as integer handles so the trace stays JSON. next is only called when hasNext is true.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Return values of add/remove, the iterator-as-handle modelling and re-add ordering are inferred.

problems.title: Split Drainage Tree

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: parent[0] = -1 and the parents form a rooted tree; input[i] is water entering at node i. Cutting one pipe (node i to parent[i], i != 0) splits the system into two; return the minimum possible absolute difference between the total water of the two parts.
problems.inference_uncertainty: The second array and the minimise-difference objective are inferred from the title; the preview cuts off after parent.

problems.title: ToDo List with Task Dependencies

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: add ignores an existing id. get returns [id, description, status] or []. updateStatus returns false for unknown ids. addDependency records that taskId requires dependsOnId; it returns false if either id is unknown, they are equal, or the edge already exists. getDependencies returns direct prerequisites in insertion order ([] if unknown).
problems.inference_uncertainty: Only add/get are visible; updateStatus and the dependency methods with their return values are inferred.

problems.title: Travese and Merge Two N-ary Trees

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Row 0 is the root; each row is [key, value, child row indices...]. Return [key, value] pairs in pre-order (node, then children left to right).
problems.inference_uncertainty: Traversal order (pre-order chosen) and output shape are inferred; root at row 0 is assumed.

problems.title: Travese and Merge Two N-ary Trees

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Both trees use the row format; sibling keys are unique and the roots share a key. Merge: matched nodes sum their values; children are A's children in order (each merged with B's same-key sibling if any) followed by B's unmatched children in order. Return the merged tree in the same row format, rows numbered in pre-order with the root at 0.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Matching rule (by key among siblings), value combination (sum) and output numbering are inferred.

problems.title: URL Maze Traversal

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: The request helper is modelled as an injected map url -> {message, next}; an unknown url responds {message: "Not Found", next: []}. Breadth-first from "/", each url requested at most once in discovery order (next lists left to right); return the first url whose message is "Congrats", or "" if none is reachable.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Return value ("" when no exit) and Not Found modelling are inferred; the HTTP helper is replaced by a deterministic map.

problems.title: URL Maze Traversal

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: As variant 1, but an entry may carry "headers" (sent with requests to the urls it discovers; first discovery wins; "/" gets an empty map) and "requiredHeaders" (if any required pair is missing or different, the response is {message: "Unauthorized", next: []}).
problems.inference_uncertainty: Highest among the multi-variant groups: the preview only says variant 1 sends empty headers; header propagation and authorization rules are invented to give headers a role.

problems.title: User Journey Paths

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Per user, order actions by the integer value of timestamp and insert the sequence into a trie; a node's count is the number of users whose journey passes through that prefix. Return one line per node (root excluded) in pre-order with children in ascending action order: two spaces per depth below the first level, then "<action> (<count>)".
problems.inference_uncertainty: Line format and child ordering are not visible (the preview ends at "formatting rules"); both are inferred.

problems.title: Variadic Function Matching

preview.scope: group-level partial public preview; not a variant specification

problems.inferred_spec: Non-variadic functions match an argument type list exactly. A variadic function (at least one parameter) matches when the arguments start with its parameter list and every extra argument has the last parameter's type (its last parameter appears one or more times). findMatches returns matching names sorted ascending. Names are unique.
problems.inference_uncertainty: Whether the variadic tail may be empty (chosen: no), result ordering and the register signature are inferred.
